out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Raw beef, raw chicken, tofu, and raw produce was all being stored in the walk-in refrigerator on the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOOD MUSTBE STORED AT LEAST 6 INHCES OFF THE GROUND AT ALL TIMES. PLEASE MAKE SURE ALL FOOD IS STORED OFF OF THE GROUND BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Packaged Food Display, No Direct Contact Water/Ice
violations.observation: The following packaged food was found stored in direct contact with ice: a bottle of lime juice and a bottle of guava juice were being stored in the ice machine with direct contact with the ice.
violations.corrective_action: Packaged food may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the food is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water.EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT PRE PACKAGED GOODS ARE NEVER ALLOWED TO BE STORED IN THE ICE MACHINE. PIC REMOVED THE TWO BOTTLES OF JUICE FROM THE ICE MACHINE.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink next to the dish washer being used to dump food from dirty dishes.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT HAND WASHING SINKS CAN ONLY BE USED TO WASH HANDS AND NOTHING ELSE. PIC CLEANED THE FOOD FROM THE SINK.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: raw beef was sitting out on a prep table to thaw.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THE 3 WAYS IN WHICH FOOD CAN BE PROPERLY THAWED. PIC BEGAN COOKING THE RAW BEEF FROM A FROZEN STATE.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the chlorine-based sanitizing solution was observed to be at a concentration less than what is required for effective sanitization of food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils. Observed the sanitizing solution of the chemical dish machine with a concentration of 0 ppm total chlorine.
violations.corrective_action: A chlorine-based sanitizing solution shall have a minimum concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine when tested using the appropriate test kit. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT THE CHEMICAL DISH MACHINE NEEDS TO BE READING AT 50 TO 200 PPM TO BE CONSIDERED WORKING PROPERLY. EHS WAS UNABLE TO GET A READING HIGHER THEN 0 PPM AFTER RUNNING THE DISH MACHINE 3 TIMES. PIC SET UP THE THREE VAT SINK IN ORDER TO WASH DISHES AND ALSO CALLED THE COMPANY THAT DOES MAINTENANCE ON THE DISHWASHER.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: raw beef and pork were thawing in standing water at the time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC NOW UNDERSTANDS THE PROPER WAYS OF THAWING FOOD. EHS PROVIDED MORE INFORMATION ON THAWING FOR PIC. PIC BEGAN TO RUN WATER AT 70F AT THE PREP SINK WHERE THE RAW BEEF AND PORK WERE THAWING.
